title: Visible and invisible (CCC 325–327)
hookLine: heaven and earth, angels and all that is

cards: Take stock of the last minute. Air you can't see went in and out of your lungs. A signal nobody can see probably carried these words to wherever you are.
Somewhere, someone's trust in you, which you can't see either, is part of why your day holds together. A lot of what holds a life up is invisible.
The Creed said at Sunday Mass calls God the maker of all things visible and invisible. Today we stay with that phrase.

teach.h: HEAVEN AND EARTH: ALL THAT EXISTS.
teach.b: Start with the bigger phrase, heaven and earth. In scripture, the Catechism says, it means all that exists: creation as a whole. The earth is the world of people.
Heaven can mean the sky, or God's own place, our Father who art in heaven, or the place of the angels around God. Then the Creed adds: visible and invisible.
Paul says it in Colossians, in the Douay-Rheims: "in him were all things created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible."

teach.h: TWO ORDERS, AND HUMANS MADE OF BOTH.
teach.b: A Church council, quoted in the Catechism, put it plainly: from the beginning God made both orders of creation, the spiritual and the bodily, the angelic and the earthly, and then the human, made of both together.
In the Catholic picture, people stand where the two orders meet: a body, like everything on earth, and a spirit. That's tomorrow, body and soul.
Invisible here doesn't mean imaginary. It means real things eyes can't catch, like the angels and the human soul.
The Creed holds that all of creation, seen and unseen, is made by God, and nothing created sits outside that making.

Look back over this week: the faith handed down, scripture at four depths, I believe inside we believe, the Creed's three movements, power as mercy, providence and its co-workers, and now the maker of all things.
In the Creed's one short phrase, the seen and the unseen stand side by side, on the same list of things made.

how: At Sunday Mass Catholics profess God as maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible, and the Church keeps feasts for the angels in its calendar.

o: the real world and the imaginary one
all things made, both seen and unseen
things known now and things still unknown

games.q: seen and unseen — tap the pairs.

s: in the Creed, invisible means imaginary
it means real things eyes can't catch, like angels and the soul.
the Catechism says heaven and earth means all that exists
Catholic teaching holds that the invisible world was never created
the Creed and the council say God made both orders, spiritual and bodily.

games.q: you're Paul, writing to the Colossians about everything Christ is over. how far do you reach?
o: only the things people can see
things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible
games.why: "in him were all things created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible." the Creed carries the same pair.

practice: Feel the air coming in, cool, then going out, warm; you've never seen it.
Now name one more invisible thing your life leans on, someone's loyalty, a promise kept, your own memory, a love you've been given, and let it be as real as the chair under you.
If you pray, thank God, maker of things seen and unseen, for it; if you don't, simply let your attention rest there.
